claims.text: The multilayer coating consists of alternating CoCrFeMnNi FCC layers and a complementary BCC high-entropy phase.
The lattices in the starting multilayer are intrinsically severely distorted.
The starting multilayer has initially uniform elastic fields.
Sustained near-creep loading of the severely distorted HEA multilayer produces localized nonlinear elastic-field undulations.
Localized elastic-field undulations act as nucleation sites for embryonic twin boundaries.
Embryonic twin-boundary formation progressively accommodates plastic deformation.
The relevant elastic-field undulations and embryonic twin-boundary features have characteristic spacings of 1–2 nm.
The elastic undulations coalesce into embryonic twin boundaries.
Twin-mediated strain accommodation enables gradual plastic flow through progressive distributed deformation rather than abrupt dislocation-slip events.
Samples displaying the proposed process will develop nanoscale twin-related features gradually under sustained loading.
The evolution of twin-related features will correlate with smoother strain-accommodation curves.
Baseline multilayers lacking pronounced elastic-field undulations exhibit abrupt yielding without evolving nanoscale twin precursors.
The proposed mechanism is limited to compositionally complex HEA multilayers with significant lattice distortion under stresses near the creep threshold.
The mechanism may not apply outside the specified material and loading regimes.
Detecting and quantifying 1–2 nm elastic-field undulations is technically challenging.
